name: Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Rotator Cuff Related Shoulder Pain
definition: Shoulder pain related to rotator-cuff tendons and associated subacromial structures, usually diagnosed clinically; structural imaging findings may exist without symptoms.

typical: Pain with overhead or reaching activity

redFlags.item: Acute traumatic inability to raise the arm with suspected major tear

investigations.principle: Imaging is not routinely required initially.
investigations.MRI: Ultrasound/MRI is appropriate for significant weakness, trauma, failed rehabilitation or surgical planning.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs can identify arthritis or calcific disease.

green: Activity modification and graded return to overhead function
amber: Injection or surgical options require individualized assessment; repeated corticosteroid exposure should be used cautiously.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-shoola symptom correlation may be documented; tendon pathology remains a modern diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Shoulder pain related to rotator-cuff tendons and associated subacromial structures, usually diagnosed clinically; structural imaging findings may exist without symptoms.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.
